learn.canDo: Explain why instructions and user input are not separable, layer defences, and limit what an injection can reach.
learn.why: Prompt injection is the top-ranked LLM risk. Interviewers expect you to say filters are not a boundary.
learn.keyIdea: Assume the prompt will be read out loud.

learn.canDo: Describe attacks carried by retrieved content, estimate exposure from retrieval volume, and contain them by quarantining and restricting actions.
learn.why: Agents that read untrusted content and act are the real attack surface. This is how you reason about it.

learn.canDo: List the channels a hijacked agent can use to move data out and close them in rendering and tools.
learn.why: Stealing needs a channel. Closing channels beats detecting intent.

learn.canDo: Add up an agent's worst case from its grants and cut it with narrow tools and scoped, short-lived credentials.
learn.why: Least privilege holds even when the model fails. It is the control interviewers want to hear.
learn.keyIdea: The permissions list is the blast radius.

chapter.story: A security review of the assistant finds that anyone who can write text it reads can steer it.
outcomes: Explain direct and indirect prompt injection
Close the channels data can leave through
Scope tools and credentials to cap the worst case
chapter.why: A model follows text, and text comes from strangers. Security here means limiting what a fooled model can reach, not trusting it to resist.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can threat-model an agent. At work you will review an agent's tools and credentials for blast radius.
